messages:
maya (prodinfra): Quick heads-up — we had a customer report where Dedicated ran out of slots and traffic got routed to Hosted, but their contract requires isolation. We need a playbook + console affordance to prevent silent evictions or at least surface them clearly.
kevin (platform): ugh. do we have a tenant-level flag that prevents automatic runaway spill to hosted? i thought we had 'allow_spillover' but not user-visible.
maya (prodinfra): yeah there's an internal flag, but it's binary and buried. proposal: add a per-tenant "eviction_mode" with values ["block","notify-only","fallback"], show it in console, and expose in the admin API.
olga (security): +1 for explicit mode. also need audit trail and proofs for compliance customers — if we ever route to hosted we must record rationale, timestamp, and model variant used.
dan (eng-runtime): technically doable. runtime already emits fallback events but not tied to tenant config. we'd need a small change: routing decision records -> {tenant_id, decision, variant, reason, kernel_hint}. e.g.

```
POST /internal/routing/decision
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-inc",
  "decision": "fallback_to_hosted",
  "variant": "gpt-3.5-q4",
  "reason": "dedicated_capacity_exhausted",
  "timestamp": 1749203456
}
```

kevin (platform): also UX: in the tenant page show a real-time "overflow" metric and last-eviction time. And surface a suggested remediation: bump reserved GPUs / enable burst pool / change eviction_mode.
pri (sre): we should tie telemetry to alerts. threshold idea: if fallback_rate > 0.5% over 5m for a tenant -> page oncall + create ticket with stack trace + recent requests sample.
maya (prodinfra): agreed. and for rollout UX: when changing eviction_mode, warn about behavioral change and require a second click to confirm for "block" -> we might reject requests if set incorrectly.
olga (security): for "block" mode we need a deterministic client-facing error code and a documented SLO hit: e.g., 429 with header X-Redwood-Evicted: true and body {code: "DEDICATED_EVICTED", guidance: "contact support or enable fallback"}.
dan (eng-runtime): implementing the header + structured error is trivial. but caveat: some customers use tool-calling; we must include a structured metadata blob so SDKs can gracefully fall back on client side.
kevin (platform): internal API shape suggestion (backwards compatible): add query param ?routing_policy=eviction_mode and a response field routing_info:{policy:..., decision:..., variant:...}. sample:

```
GET /v1/requests/submit?routing_policy=block
{
  "input": "..."
}

response: 409 + {
  "error": "DEDICATED_CAPACITY_BLOCKED",
  "routing_info": {"policy":"block","decision":"deny","timestamp":1749203501}
}
```

maya (prodinfra): this also solves audit needs. audit logs + tenant UI + alerting. timeline? can't be disruptive for this week's critical routing release. can we scope to gradable rollout?
pri (sre): safe rollout plan: (1) emit routing decision events only (no change in behavior) for 1 week, (2) expose UI read-only, (3) add error code + opt-in header via feature flag, (4) flip GA after customer trials. each step gated by canaries.
kevin (platform): ok. dan/pri — can you pair on the event schema and the dashboard tiles? i'll pick up the console copy + confirm admin API.
dan (eng-runtime): yes. i'll open an RFC with schema and sample payloads. expecting a small runtime patch.
rollout-bot: deploy v0.3.12 of routing-service completed to canary (3 hosts) — monitoring: 0 errors so far. :rocket:
kevin (platform): thanks. maya i'll draft the tenant communication and add the "eviction_mode" toggle to the admin API spec.
maya (prodinfra): awesome. one more ask: add a per-variant "fallback_score" in telemetry so we can see which quantized/cheaper variants are being chosen during evictions. helps with quality/regression checks.
dan (eng-runtime): good call. we'll include variant_quality_score and latency_estimate in the event.
olga (security): ensure KMS audit events for any hosted cross-over for regulated tenants.
kevin (platform): noted. will create a checklist for compliance-only flows.
maya (prodinfra): sweet. I'll create the Jira with the rollout plan and link it here. thanks all :thumbsup:\"
